ev.q: This report describes the patient's clinical history and the epidemiologic and laboratory investigations.
Paired whole blood specimens from the original donations had been retained from all 34 RBC donors
PCR and IFA tests on samples from a female RBC donor aged 64 years were positive for A. phagocytophilum infection
No whole blood samples from other tested donors were PCR positive for A. phagocytophilum .
Available postdonation serum samples from other donors were negative for A. phagocytophilum by IFA
this is the first published report in which transfusion transmission of A. phagocytophilum was confirmed by testing of the recipient and a donor.
Memorial Blood Centers began an investigation to identify whether any of the 59 blood donors associated with the 34 RBC

methods_quotes.q: The whole blood specimens retained from initial donation were tested by PCR, followed by sequencing of the PCR amplicons at CDC.
Serum and plasma specimens were tested by IFA for IgG antibodies to A. phagocytophilum .
IFA titers 1:64 and higher were considered positive.
